papers.title_zh: ETI治疗下停用与继续每日雾化黏液活性治疗的非劣效性随机试验（CF STORM）：52周ppFEV1达非劣效，但停药组肺部急性加重增多
papers.title_en: Stopping versus continuing nebulised mucoactive therapy in people with cystic fibrosis established on elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor (CF STORM): a multicentre, registry-based, randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial.
papers.authors: Davies G, Jones AP, Brayshaw E, Cooper R, Allen L, Bradley JM, Cameron RA, Carr SB et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: UCL Great Ormond Street Institute of Child Health, London, UK; Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Foundation …
papers.authors_conclusion: Stopping nebulised mucoactive therapy was non-inferior to continuing treatment. Registry-recorded pulmonary exacerbations were more common in the STOP group than the CONTINUE group. These data provide evidence that discontinuing nebulised mucoactive therapy is unlikely to result in worsening respiratory function for people with cystic fibrosis established on ETI aged 6 years and older with a baseline percent predicted FEV1 of at least 40%. A more cautious approach is recommended for people with ppFEV1 of 40-69%.
papers.ai_note: 结论主要建立在主要终点（ppFEV1非劣效）之上，而停药组急性加重风险显著升高(IRR 1·34, 95% CI 1·06-1·71)属次要终点且被作者表述为'更常见'而非治疗失败；两项急性加重终点方向一致但需静脉抗生素者CI跨1。建议对ppFEV1 40-69%人群'更谨慎'的表述在摘要中无对应亚组效应量与交互检验数据，属信息不足，无法核实该限定的依据。开放标签设计下肺功能为客观测量但急性加重判定依赖注册库记录，可能存在记录/报告偏倚；主要分析人群(390/591)与全随机人群的差异及其对非劣效结论的影响未说明，信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Reducing treatment burden is a priority for people with cystic fibrosis and their families. Daily nebulised therapies are a substantial treatment burden. The CF STORM study aimed to assess whether cessation of daily nebulised mucoactive therapy (dornase alfa, hypertonic saline, or both) was non-inferior to continuing treatment in people with cystic fibrosis established on the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CTFR) modulator elexacaftor plus tezacaftor plus ivacaftor (ETI). METHODS: CF STORM was a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial, done across 40 adult or paediatric specialist cystic fibrosis centres in the UK. Eligible participants were aged 6 years or older with cystic fibrosis who were established on ETI treatment for at least 3 months, with a percentage predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1) of at least 40%. Eligibility assessment, consent, randomisation, and data collection were all done within the UK Cystic Fibrosis Registry. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; using computer-generated random permuted blocks stratified by site and current mucoactive treatment) to stop their prescribed therapy (STOP) or continue their prescribed daily nebulised mucoactive therapy (dornase alfa, hypertonic saline, or both; CONTINUE). The primary outcome was change in ppFEV1 from baseline to 52 weeks (prespecified visit windows 51-55 weeks) assessed in all participants with primary outcome data. A non-inferiority margin of -3 percentage points was established for the difference between groups in ppFEV1. Safety was assessed in all randomly assigned participants who received at least one day of allocated treatment. This study is registered with the ISRCTN registry, ISRCTN14081521. FINDINGS: Between July 8, 2021, and Aug 6, 2024, 1716 people were screened. Of 684 patients eligible for enrolment, 591 were randomly assigned to either the STOP group (n=297) or the CONTINUE group (n=294). Median age was 15·5 years (IQR 12·7-29·4) and mean baseline ppFEV1 was 89·4% (SD 18·2). Stopping mucoactive therapy was non-inferior to continuing treatment for change in ppFEV1 from baseline to 52 weeks in the primary analysis population (STOP n=195, CONTINUE n=195; unadjusted mean change 0·15 [SD 6·85] ppFEV1 in STOP vs -0·79 [SD 8·01] in CONTINUE; adjusted mean difference 0·97 percentage points, 95% CI -0·51 to 2·45). Pulmonary exacerbations were more frequent in the STOP group than the CONTINUE group (incidence 0·90 vs 0·67 per person-year; incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1·34, 95% CI 1·06 to 1·71), but no significant differences were identified between groups in pulmonary exacerbations leading to treatment with intravenous antibiotic therapy (incidence 0·12 vs 0·08 per person-year; IRR 1·55, 95% CI 0·78 to 3·08). No serious adverse reactions to dornase alfa or related serious adverse events associated with hypertonic saline were reported. One death, unrelated to the study intervention, occurred in the STOP group. INTERPRETATION: Stopping nebulised mucoactive therapy was non-inferior to continuing treatment. Registry-recorded pulmonary exacerbations were more common in the STOP group than the CONTINUE group. These data provide evidence that discontinuing nebulised mucoactive therapy is unlikely to result in worsening respiratory function for people with cystic fibrosis established on ETI aged 6 years and older with a baseline percent predicted FEV1 of at least 40%. A more cautious approach is recommended for people with ppFEV1 of 40-69%. FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research Health Technology Assessment Programme, Cystic Fibrosis Trust, and UK Research and Innovation.

papers.title_zh: 晚期非小细胞肺癌血浆NGS在真实世界中发现16.8%组织未检出的可操作基因改变，拷贝数变异不稳定谱与更短OS相关（HR 1.49）
papers.title_en: Plasma-Based Genetic Characterization in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: From Real-World Evidence to Prognostic Stratification.
papers.authors: Dal Maso A, Grassi A, Bao LC, Boscolo Bragadin A, Padovan A, Alam MA, Benetti B, Mulargiu C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Medical Oncology 2 Veneto Institute of Oncology IOV - IRCCS Padova Italy.
papers.authors_conclusion: 血浆NGS证实了其在刻画晚期NSCLC更细致基因图谱以指导个体化临床实践中的价值。UCP/SCP二分类具有预后作用，可进一步用于风险分层研究。
papers.ai_note: 回顾性单中心、无外部验证：SVM分类器似在同一批数据中建立并评估，摘要未提及独立验证集或交叉验证方式，17.6%的UCP比例与预后关联可能被乐观放大。未报告任何HR的95%CI，仅给P值，精度信息不足。UCP与OS的关联可能混杂于体瘤负荷、治疗线数与进展状态，摘要未说明这些协变量是否纳入校正。16.8%的'组织未检出AGA'未区分是真新发现还是取样/检测灵敏度差异，也未说明对治疗决策的实际改变比例。次要/探索性定位与结论中'可用于风险分层'的表述之间存在跨度，属结论外推。
papers.abstract_en: Plasma next-generation sequencing (NGS) is increasingly used in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (aNSCLC), primarily to detect actionable genetic alterations (AGAs). This study aims to depict its role in a real-world setting and to test a novel support vector machine (SVM) classifier of copy number alteration (CNA) profiles as a new prognostic tool. We retrospectively collected clinico-pathological data from aNSCLC patients undergoing plasma NGS according to clinical practice at the Veneto Institute of Oncology. The primary endpoints were to describe tissue-undetected AGAs and assess the potential prognostic impact of CNA profile binary classification on overall survival (OS). 364 aNSCLC patients consecutively undergoing plasma NGS with a commercial panel were included. New AGAs were found in 61 patients (16.8%). Among 341 cases analyzed by the SVM classifier, 60 (17.6%) had an unstable CNA profile (UCP). UCP patients experienced significantly shorter OS than those with a stable profile (p = 0.026). In multivariable left-truncated Cox regression, UCP confirmed an independent adverse prognostic role both across the full cohort (HR = 1.49, p = 0.021) and within non-oncogene-addicted patients (HR = 1.86, p = 0.002). Plasma NGS confirmed its value in defining a more detailed genetic picture of aNSCLC to guide personalized clinical practice. UCP/SCP binary classification had a prognostic role and can be studied for risk stratification.

papers.title_en: Mature 4-year outcomes and exploratory postoperative ctDNA associations after sintilimab-based neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in resectable ESCC.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Wang H, Qian Y, Guo Y, Zhu M, Wen L, Xu L, Zhou G et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, The Affiliated Cancer Hospital of Nanjing Medical University, Nanjing, Jiangsu, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: Mature follow-up of this single-arm cohort describes heterogeneous long-term outcomes after sintilimab-based neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. MPR and postoperative ctDNA were associated with subsequent outcomes, whereas the pCR-within-MPR analysis remained imprecise. These exploratory findings require prospective validation.
papers.ai_note: 单臂无对照，4年OS/RFS不能归因于治疗本身，缺少同期化疗或历史对照基线；MPR与生存的关联属非随机的疗效替代终点相关性，存在混杂；12个月ctDNA分析仅3例阳性、n=28，作者已标明为描述性；MPR内pCR分析仅6个事件、CI跨1且极宽，阴性/不精确结果被如实报告但易被摘要中HR 0.12、ctDNA HR 5-6等醒目数字掩盖；ctDNA与结局均为探索性、样本量小，需前瞻验证（作者亦承认）。信息不足：未报告对照组、治疗相关不良反应及复发模式分布。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade plus chemotherapy improves pathological response in resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, but mature survival and postoperative relapse biomarkers remain incompletely defined. We report long-term follow-up of a phase II trial of sintilimab-based neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. METHODS: This mature follow-up included all 47 treated patients; 45 underwent esophagectomy, and 2 declined surgery. Overall survival (OS) was analyzed from treatment initiation in the full treated/intention-to-treat population, and recurrence-free survival (RFS) from surgery in the surgical cohort. Associations with major pathological response (MPR) and primary-tumor pathological complete response (pCR) were exploratory. Postoperative circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) was assessed using protocol-window-end landmarks at 1 and 12 months and a protocol-window-updated time-dependent RFS sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: At a median follow-up of 58.3 months, 17 deaths occurred among 47 treated patients; 4-year OS was 66.0% (95% CI 53.7% to 81.0%). Among 45 surgical patients, 4-year RFS was 46.7% (95% CI 34.1% to 63.8%), with 24 RFS events, including 22 recurrences. MPR was associated with OS (HR 0.12, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.52) and RFS (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.70). Within MPR, the post hoc pCR versus non-pCR comparison was imprecise (RFS HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.08 to 2.38; six events) and did not support equivalence. At the 1-month window-end ctDNA landmark (n=42), positivity was associated with higher hazards of death (HR 5.43, 95% CI 1.66 to 17.72) and an RFS event (HR 5.67, 95% CI 2.31 to 13.96). The strict 12-month window-end analysis (n=28; three positive) was descriptive; the protocol-window-updated time-dependent RFS analysis was consistent (HR 6.78, 95% CI 2.55 to 18.03). CONCLUSIONS: Mature follow-up of this single-arm cohort describes heterogeneous long-term outcomes after sintilimab-based neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. MPR and postoperative ctDNA were associated with subsequent outcomes, whereas the pCR-within-MPR analysis remained imprecise. These exploratory findings require prospective validation. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR1900026593.

papers.title_zh: 基于12项血清蛋白的IPF多标志物风险评分开发与验证：推导AUC 0.809，外部验证降至0.711且特异度仅0.430
papers.title_en: Multi-biomarker risk score for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis based on serum proteins by the Prognostic Lung Fibrosis Consortium (PROLIFIC): a risk score development and validation study.
papers.authors: Schafer PH, Rassa J, Seyda A, Hersey S, Eisinger D, Melin J, Bencher R, Tremaine T et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Bristol Myers Squibb, Princeton, NJ, USA; PROLIFIC Consortium, Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation, Chicago, IL, USA.
papers.authors_conclusion: 多标志物算法证实了既往分析中重要的血清蛋白，并产生了针对IPF移植自由生存与FVC下降的患者级预后风险评分；PROLIFIC风险评分已被纳入美国FDA生物标志物资格认定项目，作为IPF患者预后生物标志物，用于识别1年内更可能发生临床事件或疾病进展的患者，可作为临床试验的分层因素或入组标准。
papers.ai_note: 验证队列AUC由0·809降至0·711，且Youden指数下特异度仅0·430，提示泛化能力有限，但作者结论侧重强调AUC与FDA资格认定而未讨论验证端特异度下降。复合终点在两队列构成差异大：推导队列仅3%发生≥10%ppFVC下降，验证队列为14%；验证队列死亡仅6例、移植0例，移植自由生存部分几乎无事件支撑。验证人群为试验安慰剂组，与推导的真实世界注册队列来源不同。人群高度偏倚（推导队列94%白人、74%男性；验证队列73%白人、84%男性），外推性存疑。Youden指数敏感度/特异度为同一数据上的最优切点估计，未见独立于AUC的校准度或决策曲线报告，信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Despite decades of research, clinicians still do not have approved prognostic biomarkers that can help predict how quickly idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) will progress in individual patients. The Prognostic Lung Fibrosis Consortium (PROLIFIC) was formed to develop well-qualified assays suitable for use as prognostic biomarkers within the context of clinical trials for IPF. METHODS: For this risk score development and validation study, assays were developed for 12 peripheral blood biomarkers discovered in previous studies, representing epithelial damage (CYFRA 21-1, SP-D, CA-125, CA-19-9, and KL-6), fibrosis (MMP-7, TNC, and POSTN), inflammation (CCL18, CXCL13, and sICAM-1), and thrombosis (PAI-1), and used for IPF patient baseline serum measurements within the derivation dataset (Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation [PFF] Patient Registry; n=657) and the validation dataset (placebo groups of the ISABELA studies; n=229). The PFF Patient Registry enrolled patients in the USA (start date March 29, 2016; data cutoff Nov 30, 2022). ISABELA 1 (NCT03711162) enrolled patients in Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Chile, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Greece, Japan, Peru, Spain, Taiwan, Türkiye, the UK, and the USA (start date Nov 28, 2018; completed March 30, 2021). ISABELA 2 (NCT03733444) enrolled patients in Argentina, Canada, France, Germany, Hungary, Israel, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Poland, South Africa, South Korea, and the USA (start date Nov 5, 2018; completed March 30, 2021). Single and multi-marker statistical analyses were performed for transplant-free survival and forced vital capacity (FVC) decline at 1 year, adjusting for sex, age, BMI, antifibrotic medication, smoking pack-years, percent predicted FVC (ppFVC), and percent predicted diffusion capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide. Penalised logistic regression was used to select prognostic biomarkers using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator method, and the resulting model was used to derive a multi-marker risk score. The performance of the PROLIFIC risk score was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and by the sensitivity and specificity of the Youden Index. FINDINGS: In 657 participants in the PFF Patient Registry IPF derivation cohort, the mean age was 70·69 years (SD 8·08), 168 (26%) were female, 489 (74%) were male, 617 (94%) were White, ten (2%) were Black, 14 (2%) were Asian, and 16 (2%) were other race. A 10% or higher absolute decline of ppFVC within 1 year occurred in 20 (3%) of 657 patients. Overall longitudinal FVC decline was significantly associated with baseline MMP-7, SP-D, KL-6, PAI-1, CA19-9, CYFRA 21-1, CXCL13, and sICAM-1. Death (62 [9%] of 657 patients) or lung transplant (37 [6%] of 657 patients) within 1 year was significantly associated with baseline SP-D, sICAM-1, TNC, and KL-6. A multi-marker prognostic model or PROLIFIC risk score for the composite outcome of death, lung transplant, or at least 10% absolute decline in ppFVC at 1 year was associated with baseline SP-D, CXCL13, sICAM-1, TNC, and CA-125 (derivation area under the curve [AUC] 0·809 [95% CI 0·763-0·855]; Youden Index sensitivity 0·643 and specificity 0·847). In 229 participants in the ISABELA study validation cohort, the mean age was 70·08 years (SD 6·79), 36 (16%) were female, 193 (84%) were male, 168 (73%) were White, one (<1%) was Black, 53 (23%) were Asian, and 7 (3%) were other race. A 10% or higher absolute decline of ppFVC occurred in 31 (14%) of 229 patients, death in six (3%) of 229 patients, and lung transplant in zero patients within 1 year. The performance of the PROLIFIC risk score was tested in this validation cohort (AUC 0·711 [95% CI 0·614-0·808]; Youden Index sensitivity 0·820 and specificity 0·430). INTERPRETATION: A multi-marker algorithm confirmed the important serum proteins consistent with findings from previous analyses and yielded a patient-level prognostic risk score for transplant-free survival and FVC decline in IPF. The PROLIFIC risk score has been accepted into the US Food and Drug Administration Biomarker Qualification Program as a prognostic biomarker in patients with IPF to identify patients who are more likely to have clinical events or disease progression within 1 year and to be used as a stratification factor or as an eligibility criterion in clinical trials. FUNDING: The Prognostic Lung Fibrosis Consortium.

papers.title_en: Association of BMI with type 2 biomarkers, asthma burden, and severe asthma attack risk: an analysis of control groups of the ORACLE2 patient-level meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Riemann S, Meulmeester FL, Mailhot-Larouche S, Wechsler ME, Diver SE, Brightling CE, Castro M, Hanania NA et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory Medicine, Ghent University Hospital, Ghent, Belgium; Department of Epidemiology, Eramus MC, Ro…
papers.authors_conclusion: Most patients with obesity-related asthma have evidence of type 2 inflammation despite a modest shift towards type 2-low disease. High BMI is associated with increased asthma burden and attack risk. These findings support a multidimensional view of obesity-associated asthma, in which type 2 inflammation frequently coexists with obesity-related mechanisms that independently contribute to disease burden and asthma attack risk.
papers.ai_note: 发作风险仅报告重度肥胖（BMI≥40）这一显著亚组，超重组与总体肥胖组的率比未在摘要中给出，存在只强调显著亚组的选择性呈现风险；重度肥胖组校正后CI接近1（1.06–2.33），且肥胖患者基线更常处于GINA 5级治疗、既往发作与肺功能差异大，残余混杂与指征混杂难以完全排除；'82%仍有2型炎症'系由18%的2型低反推，属推导性表述而非直接测量；对照组为试验人群，外推至一般哮喘门诊人群受限。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Obesity-related asthma is frequently described as a type 2-low phenotype, but data on type 2 biomarker distributions across BMI and their relationship with asthma attack risk are scarce. We aimed to examine the distribution of type 2 biomarkers across BMI categories in adolescents and adults with asthma and to investigate how BMI relates to risk of severe attacks. METHODS: We analysed data from the ORACLE2 patient-level meta-analysis of control groups of 22 randomised placebo-controlled asthma trials, previously identified through a systematic review of MEDLINE from Jan 1, 1993, to April 1, 2021. We estimated annualised severe asthma attack rate ratios using negative binomial models, adjusted for sex, age, blood eosinophil count (BEC), fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), percent predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 s (ppFEV1), percent predicted forced vital capacity, treatment step, previous severe attacks, and trial. FINDINGS: In the ORACLE2 patient-level meta-analysis (n=6513), 2393 (37%) of 6513 participants with asthma had overweight (BMI 25 kg/m2 to <30 kg/m2) and 2723 (42%) had obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2). Those with obesity had highest symptom burden, lowest baseline ppFEV1, and were most frequently on Global Initiative for Asthma step 5 treatment. Although the proportion of patients with dual type 2-high biomarkers (BEC ≥0·3 × 109 cells per L and FeNO ≥35 parts per billion) was lower in the obese versus normal BMI group (15% vs 26%; p<0·0001), the proportion of type 2-low asthma (BEC <0·15 × 109 cells per L and FeNO <20 ppb) was higher (18% vs 13%; p<0·0001), indicating that 82% of asthma patients with obesity still have some degree of type 2 inflammation. Compared with normal BMI, severe obesity (BMI ≥40 kg/m2) was associated with a significantly higher asthma attack risk (adjusted rate ratio 1·57, 95% CI 1·06-2·33). INTERPRETATION: Most patients with obesity-related asthma have evidence of type 2 inflammation despite a modest shift towards type 2-low disease. High BMI is associated with increased asthma burden and attack risk. These findings support a multidimensional view of obesity-associated asthma, in which type 2 inflammation frequently coexists with obesity-related mechanisms that independently contribute to disease burden and asthma attack risk. FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research, Oxford Biomedical Research Centre, Association Pulmonaire du Québec, Fonds de Recherche du Québec-Santé, Academy of Medical Sciences, and Ghent University Special Research Fund.

papers.title_en: Optimizing early and locally advanced NSCLC: A Portuguese expert consensus on treatment pathways.
papers.authors: Dias M, Simões S, Estevinho F, Travancinha C, Rodrigues C, Paupério GS, Cardia JL, Alves P et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Serviço de Pneumologia, Unidade Local de Saúde Gaia Espinho, Vila Nova de Gaia, Portugal.
papers.authors_conclusion: 该研究提供了首个葡萄牙早期及局部晚期NSCLC专家共识，提供循证建议和实用算法以标准化诊疗并改善结局，同时将国际证据适配至本国情境；未来工作应聚焦数字临床落地并将方法拓展至转移性疾病。
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：未报告共识方法学细节（投票轮次、达成阈值如≥80%、共识度量、文献检索与证据分级流程），亦无参与者间一致性数据；结论中'标准化诊疗并改善结局'为无对照、无患者结局数据的预期性表述，不能视为已验证的临床获益；适用于葡萄牙医疗体系的建议向其他国家外推需谨慎。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Management of early and locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is increasingly complex due to expanding therapeutic options, requiring integration of efficacy, safety, and quality of life. As treatment options continue to evolve, structured, multidisciplinary approaches are essential. RESEARCH QUESTION: This study aims to develop tailored treatment algorithms and clinical recommendations for early and locally advanced NSCLC in Portugal. These recommendations will continue to evolve as the treatment landscape expands. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A multidisciplinary panel of 12 experts (4 pulmonologists/oncologists, 4 thoracic surgeons, 4 radiation oncologists) participated in a structured Patient Profile Think Tank. Current diagnostic, staging, and treatment strategies for early and locally advanced NSCLC were reviewed. Consensus statements were generated through iterative discussions and validated via voting. Key decision points were integrated into treatment algorithms, supported by literature. RESULTS: Consensus was reached on several key treatment decision points, including mandatory molecular testing at initial diagnosis and re-evaluation; standardised criteria for tumour resectability; and the integration of immunotherapy and targeted therapies in NSCLC. Multidisciplinary team discussions were considered essential throughout the patient pathway. CONCLUSION: This initiative provides the first Portuguese expert consensus on early and locally advanced NSCLC, offering evidence-based recommendations and practical algorithms to standardise care and improve outcomes, while adapting international evidence to the national context. Future efforts should focus on digital clinical implementation and extending approaches to metastatic disease.

papers.authors: Esteban C, Larrea-Aguirre N, Aramburu A, Chasco L, Moraza J, Aizpiri S, Aburto M, Quintana JM et al.

papers.abstract_en: RESEARCH QUESTION: The 6-minute walk test (6MWT) is a fundamental instrument in the clinical management of COPD patients, yet the prognostic value of specific physiological parameters during the recovery phase remains underexplored. This study aimed to determine whether the recovery time of oxygen saturation (SpO2-RT) following a 6MWT is associated with long-term prognosis (death and hospitalizations) in a cohort of patients with COPD. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: In this prospective observational cohort, 512 consecutive patients were recruited through the Galdakao University Hospital Respiratory Service and underwent pulmonary function and quadriceps strength assessments, multisensor accelerometry, and a 6MWT. Desaturation was defined as a ≥3% decrease in SpO2 from baseline during the 6MWT; SpO2-RT was the time from test completion until SpO2 returned to baseline. RESULTS: Of the 512 enrolled patients 25% were female. Those who experienced oxygen desaturation during the 6MWT exhibited significantly worse pulmonary function (FEV1%, RV%, IC/TLC and DLCO%) (p <.0001), higher fibrinogen levels (p =.01), lower quadriceps strength (p =.02), reduced PA (p <.0001), and a shorter distance walked (p <.0001). Within the desaturation sub-cohort, differences were analysed based on a SpO2-RT cut-off ≥ 80 seconds. Patients with a prolonged SpO2-RT exhibited more severe pulmonary function impairment (p values ranging from .02 to <.0001), significantly lower PA (p =.001), and shorter distance 6MWT (p <.0001). During the 3-year follow-up increased SpO2-RT was associated with increased mortality (p =.03) and hospitalizations (p =.0003). In the adjusted analyses, prolonged SpO2-RT was associated with an approximately twofold higher risk of both hospitalization (p = .02) and mortality (p =.04). INTERPRETATION: A prolonged SpO2-RT ≥ 80 identifies a COPD phenotype characterized by diminished respiratory reserve and an increased risk of subsequent exacerbation-related hospitalizations and all-cause mortality. SpO2-RT is a simple, accessible metric that enhances the prognostic utility of the standard 6MWT.

papers.abstract_en: The limited efficacy of EGFR-TKIs in EGFR-mutant lung cancer brain metastases often requires cytotoxic combination therapy, highlighting a distinct intracranial microenvironment that fosters drug tolerance. We identify a metabolically active senescent persister population that survives initial treatment and subsequently resumes proliferation. CRYAB supports this state by binding VDAC2, increasing ER-mitochondria contacts and mitochondrial calcium influx, and promoting DRP1-dependent fission. Genetic depletion of CRYAB or DRP1, pharmacological inhibition of fission, and selective ablation of p16-positive tumor cells delay proliferative recovery and tumor regrowth under continuous osimertinib. Surface plasmon resonance shows direct 25-hydroxycholesterol (25HC)-CRYAB binding, and a 25HC-containing diet enhances osimertinib activity and prolongs survival in preclinical models. In an exploratory 30-patient cohort, low CRYAB associates with a numerically higher intracranial objective response rate, whereas high baseline CRYAB associates with shorter intracranial progression-free survival. These findings define a CRYAB-VDAC2-mitochondrial-fission program that enables escape from therapy-induced senescence in lung cancer brain metastases.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate identification of metastatic lymph nodes (LNs) remains a major challenge in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) surgery. Single-cell RNA sequencing and multiplex immunohistochemistry reveal enrichment of fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) in metastatic LNs, providing a clinically informed target for molecular imaging. Guided by this finding, an FGFR2-targeted dual-modality probe, 18F-NOTA-(ICG)-DcP5, is engineered by integrating the cyclic peptide DcP5, indocyanine green (ICG), and a NOTA radiolabeling module within a unified molecular construct. The probe enables complementary positron emission tomography (PET) and second near-infrared-window (NIR-II) fluorescence imaging across whole-body and local operative settings, while competitive blocking supports an FGFR2-dependent targeting component. Across subcutaneous and orthotopic ESCC models, a proof-of-concept lymph node dissemination model, and metastatic LN-derived patient-derived xenografts, the imaging strategy supports lesion detection, lymph-node discrimination, and NIR-II-guided intraoperative localization. The probe achieves a NIR-II tumor-to-background ratio of 3.64 ± 0.23, exceeding clinical ICG (1.39 ± 0.20) by 162%. A rapid ex vivo incubation protocol further distinguishes metastatic from non-metastatic LNs in freshly resected human surgical specimens using histopathology as the reference standard (AUC = 0.9167). By bridging clinically informed target discovery with multimodal image-guided intervention, this work advances a precision strategy for selective lymph -node management in ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Hyperimmune intravenous immunoglobulin (hIVIG) is a preparation of polyclonal antibodies obtained from pooled convalescent plasma or immunised animals. It is a potential therapy for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). This review update focusses on hIVIG. It emanates from a 2021 parent review investigating convalescent plasma and hIVIG for people with COVID-19. OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of hIVIG therapy for people with COVID-19, and to maintain evidence currency using a living systematic review approach. SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, the Epistemonikos COVID-19 L*OVE Platform, and clinical trial registries from 1 January 2019 onwards. We conducted searches on 15 December 2024. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated hIVIG for COVID-19, irrespective of participants' disease severity, age, gender, or ethnicity. We excluded other coronavirus disease studies, and those evaluating standard immunoglobulin. OUTCOMES: We used the GRADE approach to rate the certainty of evidence for all-cause mortality, clinical status or symptom resolution, quality of life, adverse events, grade 3-4 adverse events, and serious adverse events. RISK OF BIAS: We used the RoB 2 tool to assess bias in the RCTs. SYNTHESIS METHODS: We followed standard Cochrane methodology. INCLUDED STUDIES: We included eight new RCTs in this update, for a total of 13 included studies with 3374 participants. Of these, 1511 participants received hIVIG from humans, 547 received swine glyco-humanised polyclonal antibody, 1075 received a bovine-derived polyclonal preparation, and 241 received equine-derived polyclonal antibody (EpAb). Three RCTs included participants with asymptomatic or mild disease, one included participants with mild to moderate disease, and nine included participants with moderate to severe disease. We identified eight ongoing studies and nine studies awaiting assessment. SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: We summarise key results for three prioritised comparisons below. The main review presents five comparisons (including these three) in summary of findings tables, and all analysed comparisons (including additional dose ranges of hIVIG and animal-derived polyclonal antibodies), with some results presented in supplementary tables. Participants with moderate to severe disease Benefits of human-derived hIVIG hIVIG may have little to no impact on all-cause mortality at 28 days (risk ratio (RR) 0.75, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.45 to 1.24; low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect on worsening of clinical status by day 7 (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.23; very low-certainty evidence). It may have little to no impact on improvement of clinical status by day 28 (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.08; low-certainty evidence). No studies reported on quality of life. Harms of human-derived hIVIG hIVIG may have little to no impact on adverse events (any grade) by day 28 (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.19; 449 per 1000; 2 studies, 599 participants; low-certainty evidence). Participants receiving hIVIG probably experience more grade 3-4 adverse events than those given placebo (RR 4.09, 95% CI 1.39 to 12.01; moderate-certainty evidence). hIVIG therapy may have little to no effect on serious adverse events or death by day 28 (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.45 to 1.14; 96 per 1000; 1 study, 572 participants; low-certainty evidence). Benefits of equine-derived polyclonal antibody (EpAb) EpAb may reduce all-cause mortality at 28 days (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.26 to 1.37; low-certainty evidence). EpAb may reduce worsening of clinical status by day 28 (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.38 to 1.18; low-certainty evidence). It may improve clinical status by day 28 (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.17; low-certainty evidence). No studies reported on quality of life. Harms of EpAb EpAb may have little to no impact on the number of adverse events (any grade) by day 28 (RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.31; low-certainty evidence). Grade 3-4 adverse events were not reported. EpAb may reduce serious adverse events (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.38 to 1.19; low-certainty evidence). Participants with asymptomatic or mild disease Benefits of human-derived hIVIG We do not know whether hIVIG has any impact on all-cause mortality at 28 days (RR not estimable as no events; very low-certainty evidence). hIVIG may have little to no effect on admission to hospital or death by day 28 (RR 2.38, 95% CI 0.63 to 9.03; low-certainty evidence). It may have little to no impact on symptom resolution by day 14 (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.21; low-certainty evidence). Quality of life was not reported. Harms of human-derived hIVIG hIVIG may have little to no impact on adverse events (any grade) by day 28 (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.72 to 1.18; low-certainty evidence). Grade 3-4 adverse events were not reported. hIVIG may have little to no effect on serious adverse events by day 28 (RR 2.38, 95% CI 0.63 to 9.03; low-certainty evidence). AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: We included data from 13 RCTs that compared hIVIG to standard therapy or placebo. Clinical heterogeneity (e.g. human- and animal-derived preparations, varying doses and comparators) precluded pooling most of the studies. In moderate to severe disease, human-derived hIVIG may have little to no impact on mortality or clinical improvement. hIVIG may have little to no effect on adverse events of any grade and serious adverse events, and probably increases grade 3-4 adverse events. In moderate to severe disease, equine-derived polyclonal antibody may reduce mortality and clinical worsening, and may increase the number of people discharged at 28 days. EpAb may have little to no impact on adverse events at 28 days and may reduce serious adverse events. In asymptomatic to mild disease, the effect of human-derived hIVIG on mortality is very uncertain. It may have little to no impact on symptom resolution, adverse events (any grade), and serious adverse events. This is the second and final update of this living systematic review. We regularly searched for new evidence and updated the review as relevant studies became available. With funding expired and the need for a living approach no longer urgent, the review will be retired after this update. FUNDING: European Union Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme (grant agreement No. 101015756) REGISTRATION: The protocol was registered with the Center for Open Science on 17 April 2020.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viral infections have few virus-specific biomarkers, with current monitoring relying on subjective symptoms and non-specific biomarkers (procalcitonin and C-reactive protein). Myxovirus resistance protein A (MxA), a virus-specific biomarker, has shown rapid induction (1-2 h) and a moderate half-life (approximately 2·3 days) in experimental studies, but its protein-level kinetics remain poorly characterised in individuals with naturally acquired respiratory viral infections. We investigated MxA temporal kinetics in these patients, evaluated its potential as a biomarker for monitoring infection resolution, and assessed antiviral treatment efficacy in individuals with influenza or SARS-CoV-2 infection. METHODS: This single-centre, prospective cohort study enrolled adult outpatients (aged ≥18 years) with acute respiratory viral infections from the outpatient clinic at China-Japan Friendship Hospital in Beijing between Dec 11, 2023, and March 14, 2024, with 2-3 follow-up visits within 14 days. Patients were included if they presented with at least two respiratory symptoms with a symptom duration of seven days or less. Exclusion criteria included interferon therapy within 30 days, major surgery, myocardial infarction or stroke, substantial trauma or burns, vaccination within 30 days, or unavailable study samples. Viral pathogens included influenza, SARS-CoV-2, rhinovirus, human coronaviruses, respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, parainfluenza virus, human metapneumovirus, and enterovirus. Peripheral blood samples were collected, and MxA levels were measured quantitatively using a fluorescence immunochromatography assay. Symptom severity, virological data, and antiviral treatment regimens were documented. Generalised estimating equation (GEE) models were used to assess the dynamic relationships between MxA levels, viral reads measured by multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing (mp-tNGS), and symptom severity, and the effects of antiviral treatments on MxA trajectories. FINDINGS: A total of 201 outpatients with respiratory viral infections (59 influenza A, 43 influenza B, 78 SARS-CoV-2, 21 other viruses) with a median age of 34 years (41 for SARS-CoV-2) were included in this study. MxA levels were high on the day of symptom onset (median 116·0 ng/mL; IQR 84·7-166·0), peaked around day 2, and gradually decreased, falling below 50 ng/mL by day 10. SARS-CoV-2 showed significantly faster MxA decline than did influenza (p<0·0001). Multivariable GEE models showed that longitudinal changes in viral reads measured by mp-tNGS correlated positively and significantly with MxA levels (estimate=18·0; 95% confidence interval [CI], 10·4-25·7; p<0·0001). MxA correlated with mean total symptom scores (estimate=0·0029; 95% CI, 0·0018-0·0041; p<0·0001) and systemic symptom scores (estimate=0·0045; 95% CI, 0·0029-0·0060; p<0·0001), with strongest associations in the early infection phase. MxA levels also correlated positively with the mean respiratory symptom scores (estimate=0·0023; 95% CI, 0·0009-0·0038; p=0·0015). In individuals with influenza B, MxA levels declined significantly faster when treated with baloxavir compared with oseltamivir (estimate=-10·8; 95% CI, -17·1 to -4·5; p=0·0008). This faster decline trend aligned with changes observed in viral reads measured by mp-tNGS and clinical symptom improvement. In individuals with SARS-CoV-2, those receiving no antiviral therapy showed significantly slower MxA decline (p=0·022). Among patients with lower respiratory viral infections who experienced fever within 48 h of blood sampling (n=48), higher baseline MxA independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality (odds ratio 1·004; 95% CI, 1·001-1·008). INTERPRETATION: Our findings indicate that temporal changes in MxA levels correlate closely with viral load and symptom severity, suggesting that MxA could serve as a potential biomarker for monitoring infection resolution in respiratory viral infections. MxA decline is slower than viral load clearance (days 7-8), which may partially reflect its half-life; MxA levels generally fell below 50 ng/mL by day 10 after symptom onset, supporting its potential utility for monitoring infection resolution. Combining MxA with viral load testing provides a more comprehensive disease assessment. Additionally, MxA could help to guide antiviral management, although further validation is required. Limitations include small subgroup sample sizes, variable enrolment timing, low participant retention, and exclusion of immunosuppressed patients. FUNDING: Beijing Research Ward Excellence Program, Department of Emergency Response, National Disease Control and Prevention Administration, China-Japan Friendship Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, National Natural Science Foundation of China, Noncommunicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, Zybio, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences (CAMS) Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences, and New Cornerstone Science Foundation. Materials for MxA measurements were provided by Zybio.

papers.abstract_en: The mechanisms driving cancer immune escape remain incompletely understood. Our study reveals that alternative RNA splicing is hyperactivated in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), particularly in the classic neuroendocrine subtypes, and is associated with poor prognosis. ASCL1, a defining transcription factor of SCLC, directly binds to and up-regulates the expression of multiple splicing factors, including PRMT5. Elevated levels of these splicing factors correlate with an increase in skipped exon (SE) events. Notably, the SEs in SCLC exhibit strong immunogenicity and are linked to immune suppression. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of PRMT5 significantly suppresses SCLC progression both in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptome analyses demonstrate that PRMT5 deficiency reduces the prevalence of SEs and mutually exclusive exons (MXEs), thereby maintaining exons with high immunogenicity. Consistent with these findings, the clinically safe PRMT5 inhibitor GSK3326595 synergizes with anti-PD1 antibody to treat SCLC by repressing alternative RNA splicing and enhancing immune responses. We conclude that hyperactive alternative RNA splicing, which excludes immunogenic exons, serves as a key mechanism for immune escape in SCLC, highlighting a potential therapeutic vulnerability for this aggressive disease.

papers.affiliation_highlight: State Key Laboratory of Genetics and Development of Complex Phenotypes, Shanghai Pudong Hospital, School of Life Science…
papers.authors_conclusion: 作者认为FT驱动的恶性肿瘤可能表现出与“凝聚体病（condensatopathy）”一致的特征，并提示癌蛋白的空间组织是精准肿瘤学中潜在的治疗脆弱靶点；同时认为对凝聚体的遗传或药理干预可消除恶性转化，FGFR3与AURKA双抑制可协同抑制肿瘤生长并诱导凝聚体溶解。
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要无任何定量结果（无效应量、CI/P、样本量、协同指数），双抑制的“协同”未给出可核查的定量依据；无人类样本或临床结局数据，FGFR3-TACC3相关结论外推至患者选择缺乏直接证据；相分离/凝聚体领域存在方法学与可重复性争议，FLIM-FRET与蛋白质组学证据的因果链（凝聚体→AURKA活化→MYC稳定→转化）在摘要层面为相关性推断，干预实验的具体设计与对照未报告，无法评估混杂与特异性（如药理工具对相变的脱靶效应）。
papers.abstract_en: Recurrent FGFR3-TACC3 (FT) fusions are potent oncogenic drivers in glioblastoma and lung cancer, yet the biophysical basis of their signaling potency remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that FT fusions undergo liquid-liquid phase separation to form membrane-tethered condensates on endoplasmic reticulum. Driven by the TACC3 coiled-coil domain, these condensates function as specialized signaling hubs that enhance FGFR3 native kinase activity and promote hyperactivation of the canonical MAPK/ERK pathway. Proteomic mapping and FLIM-FRET biosensing identify AURKA as a critical co-factor sequestered and hyperactivated within these hubs, facilitating MYC stabilization and oncogenic progression. Genetic or pharmacological intervention of these condensates abrogates malignant transformation. Furthermore, dual inhibition of FGFR3 and AURKA synergistically suppresses tumor growth and induces condensate dissolution in preclinical murine models. Our findings suggest that FT-driven malignancies may exhibit features consistent with a condensatopathy and highlight the spatial organization of oncoproteins as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in precision oncology.

papers.authors: Duan L, Hu Y, Lin H, Jian Z, Zhu J, Ren S, Yi Y, Liang J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, PR China.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Paclitaxel is a cornerstone chemotherapeutic agent for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), yet its clinical efficacy is frequently compromised by drug resistance. To address this challenge, we performed an unbiased screening approach to identify resistance-associated molecular targets with therapeutic potential. METHODS: PLAUR expression was systematically analyzed in paclitaxel-resistant ESCC cell lines, clinical ESCC specimens, and public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets. Genetic loss- and gain-of-function approaches were employed to evaluate the impact of PLAUR on paclitaxel sensitivity and apoptosis in ESCC cells. NF-κB pathway activation was assessed by transcriptomic profiling and western blot analysis. The effects of PLAUR depletion and cenupatide (UPARANT) treatment were evaluated in patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and xenograft models. RESULTS: PLAUR was consistently upregulated in paclitaxel-resistant ESCC cells, tumor tissues from poor responders, and malignant epithelial cell clusters associated with poor therapeutic response identified by single-cell analysis. Genetic ablation of PLAUR significantly enhanced paclitaxel-induced apoptosis and reduced drug resistance, whereas PLAUR re-expression conferred resistance. Mechanistically, PLAUR promoted paclitaxel resistance by activating the NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby suppressing apoptosis. Inhibition of NF-κB signaling attenuated PLAUR-associated resistance. Cenupatide enhanced paclitaxel sensitivity in the tested cell, PDO, and xenograft models. CONCLUSION: PLAUR contributes to paclitaxel resistance in ESCC through NF-κB-associated suppression of apoptosis. These preclinical findings support further evaluation of cenupatide-mediated paclitaxel sensitization in ESCC.

papers.authors: Ning D, Fu M, Khairil Anuar MA, Kue CS

papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，非系统评价；作者自述历史检索文档不完整、可复现性受限，检索时间'至2026年8月'的截止点亦无法核实。摘要中HCHTOG1906的阴性结果与CRISEC、EPOC1802的未随机化时机均无任何效应量、CI或P值，无法判断阴性结论的把握度（是否等效性设计或检验效能不足）。综述同时并列已获批适应证的阳性III期试验与时机阴性证据，易使读者将'药物有效'与'时机已明确'混同；核心建议属试验方法学框架，未提供可直接改变临床决策的时机证据。
papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have established roles in selected advanced and postoperative esophageal squamous cell carcinoma settings, but evidence supporting an immunotherapy-containing regimen does not necessarily establish its optimal initiation time. This narrative review evaluates timing within advanced, neoadjuvant, postoperative, and definitive chemoradiotherapy pathways. A targeted synthesis of the previously assembled literature through August 2026 was supplemented by separately documented citation and protocol checks; incomplete historical search documentation limits reproducibility. Evidence is classified by study design and whether initiation timing was actually randomized. Phase III trials support first-line chemoimmunotherapy in appropriate advanced-disease populations, whereas the randomized neoadjuvant HCHTOG1906 trial did not demonstrate superior pathological response or survival with cycle-day-3 versus same-day toripalimab. CRISEC and EPOC1802 used post-chemoradiotherapy schedules without randomizing start time. Biological observations and prolonged antibody activity do not identify a transferable calendar window. We propose a research framework that distinguishes established safety requirements, protocol-specific eligibility thresholds, and unvalidated recovery measurements; operationalizes subsequent-treatment completability through prespecified pathway milestones; and separates prognostic, predictive, pharmacodynamic, and safety/readiness biomarkers. Future trials should specify the population, treatment strategies, common time zero, intercurrent-event handling, and primary estimand. Failure to reach assigned treatment must remain visible in intention-to-treat analyses, while survival, disease control, treatment delivery, and patient-reported recovery require setting-specific prioritization. Established stage-specific treatment should remain the clinical reference rather than be displaced by an unvalidated timing strategy.

papers.authors: Du M, Sun Y, Fang L, Li X, Du Y, Fu J, Zha Y, Cao W et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory Medicine, Affiliated Hospital of Jiujiang University, Jiujiang, Jiangxi, China.

papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，摘要未说明系统检索策略与偏倚风险评估，纳入研究以回顾性关联为主，全部主要结果无任何效应量、CI或P值可核；作者提出前瞻性验证框架但无自身验证数据；cut-off不一致、动态监测缺乏标准化等局限由作者自陈，证据强度存在被高估的风险。
papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are an important treatment for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the lack of reliable biomarkers for outcome stratification limits their precise clinical application. Peripheral blood eosinophil-related parameters, including absolute eosinophil count (AEC), relative eosinophil count (REC) and dynamic changes during treatment, have been studied as candidate biomarkers in recent years because of their convenient detection and dynamic monitoring. At the same time, tumor tissue eosinophilia (TATE), as a direct manifestation of a local immune response, has also attracted attention. This review focuses on the clinical associations of the above indicators in the immunotherapy of NSCLC: the association between baseline AEC and REC levels and patient survival, the association of early on-treatment eosinophil elevation with clinical benefit, the association between baseline AEC and immune-related adverse events, particularly checkpoint inhibitor-related pneumonitis, and whether TATE may provide supplementary information to peripheral blood indicators. In addition, the potential role of eosinophils in the association of immune-related adverse events (irAEs) with efficacy is explored, raising the hypothesis that eosinophils may lie at the intersection of antitumor immunity and immune-mediated toxicity. Based on the available evidence, we further propose a framework for prospective validation that incorporates prespecified baseline stratification, early on-treatment dynamic monitoring, endpoint assessment, and multivariable modeling, with the aim of facilitating the transition of eosinophil-related biomarkers from retrospective associations to prospective clinical validation. In addition to clinical evidence, this paper also summarizes the potential mechanisms through which eosinophils are recruited, activated, and participate in antitumor immunity within the tumor microenvironment. Existing evidence suggests that the above indicators have potential clinical utility, but problems such as inconsistent cut-off values, lack of standardization of dynamic monitoring, and insufficient prospective verification have not yet been resolved. The NSCLC-specific mechanisms underlying eosinophil-associated effects require further investigation.

papers.authors: Xu S, Tang W, Zhu X, Guo A, Lu S, Chen Z
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, School of Medicine, Zhejiang University, No.
papers.authors_conclusion: SOX2-OT potentiates the E2F1-HES6 interaction via its molecular scaffold function, thereby suppressing NK cell function and driving immunosuppression in LUAD.
papers.ai_note: 纯临床前研究，无样本量、效应量、CI或P值等定量信息，信息不足；HES6与NK浸润相关性主要来自TIMER3.0数据库，临床标本验证的样本量与统计学数据摘要未报告；相关性不等于因果，且未证明该轴对免疫治疗应答的预测价值；过表达模型不能等同于可成药靶点干预；功能实验多为体外，体内仅报告'促进肿瘤生长、减少NK浸润'的定性结论。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) escapes immune surveillance by building an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Within that microenvironment, impaired natural killer (NK) cell function is considered an important mechanism promoting tumor progression and immune escape. However, the molecular networks that control NK cell function in LUAD remain incompletely defined. We therefore examined the role of the SOX2-OT/E2F1/HES6 axis in LUAD immunosuppression and defined its regulatory mechanism. METHODS: We used the TIMER3.0 database to analyze the correlation between HES6 and NK cell infiltration. Clinical LUAD samples were then used to validate this correlation. The effect of HES6 on NK cell function was assessed by RT-qPCR, Western blotting, flow cytometry, LDH release assay, and ELISA. ChIP, dual-luciferase reporter assays, RNA pull-down, and immunofluorescence were used to define the regulatory relationships among SOX2-OT, E2F1, and HES6. Finally, we used a tumor-bearing mouse model to test how the SOX2-OT/E2F1/HES6 axis affects tumor growth and NK cell infiltration. RESULTS: HES6 expression was prominently downregulated in LUAD and positively correlated with NK cell infiltration levels. Functional assays unveiled that HES6 overexpression potentiated NK cell cytotoxicity directly, elevated the proportion of activated NK cells, and promoted the secretion of effector cytokines IFN-γ and TNF-α. Mechanistic investigations elucidated that the transcription factor E2F1 directly integrated with the HES6 promoter and repressed its transcriptional activity. The lncRNA SOX2-OT served as a molecular scaffold to potentiate the transcriptional repression of E2F1 targeting HES6. In vivo experiments confirmed that SOX2-OT overexpression prominently facilitated tumor growth and attenuated NK cell infiltration, while co-overexpression of HES6 abrogated this effect. CONCLUSIONS: SOX2-OT potentiates the E2F1-HES6 interaction via its molecular scaffold function, thereby suppressing NK cell function and driving immunosuppression in LUAD.

papers.title_zh: Chronic stress-induced CD73 transfer by small extracellular vesicles fosters an immunosuppressive premetastatic niche for breast cancer lung metastasis.
papers.title_en: Chronic stress-induced CD73 transfer by small extracellular vesicles fosters an immunosuppressive premetastatic niche for breast cancer lung metastasis.
papers.authors: Wang M, Zhang L, Ren G, Luo K, Ke S, Ying Q, Xu Q, Hu X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Breast Surgery, The Second Affiliated Hospital Zhejiang University School of Medicine, Hangzhou, Zhejiang,…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic stress is a prevalent clinical challenge that significantly accelerates breast cancer lung metastasis. However, the precise mechanisms by which stress-induced signals are remotely communicated to the lung to facilitate premetastatic niche (PMN) formation remain poorly defined. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) play key roles in PMN establishment. CD73, an ectoenzyme enriched in sEVs, catalyzes the conversion of AMP to adenosine (ADO) and contributes to the establishment of an immunosuppressive microenvironment, emerging as an important immune checkpoint. However, whether chronic stress influences CD73+ sEVs and its role in breast cancer lung metastasis remains unclear. METHODS: A chronic restraint stress model was established in orthotopic 4T1 tumor-bearing BALB/c mice. Tumor-derived sEVs were isolated by differential ultracentrifugation and systemically administered to evaluate lung PMN formation. Flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, and ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry were used to assess immune changes and ADO production. Genetic deletion of Nt5e (encoding CD73) via CRISPR/Cas9 and pharmacologic inhibition with α, β-methyleneadenosine 5ʹ-diphosphate were applied to validate the CD73/ADO axis. The upstream regulatory mechanism was investigated using isoproterenol (ISO) stimulation, bulk RNA-seq, cholesterol-chelating agent methyl-β-cyclodextrin (MβCD), and PI3K inhibitor LY294002. RESULTS: Circulating CD73, predominantly in sEVs-associated form, was significantly elevated in chronic stressed mice, 4T1 tumor-bearing mice with higher metastatic burden, and patients with de novo lung metastatic breast cancer, underscoring its potential as a liquid biomarker. Mechanistically, chronic stress triggered Nt5e mRNA upregulation via the BAR-PI3K–AKT–HIF-1α axis while paradoxically reducing intracellular CD73 protein levels, indicating active protein mobilization into sEVs via a lipid raft-associated pathway. These circulating CD73+ sEVs were efficiently internalized by lung epithelial cells, amplifying local ADO production and establishing an immunosuppressive PMN characterized by impaired CD8+ T and NK cell activity. Genetic deletion or pharmacologic inhibition of CD73 attenuated chronic stress-induced immune suppression and markedly reduced breast cancer lung metastasis. CONCLUSIONS: Chronic stress promotes lung metastasis by transferring functional CD73 to lung epithelial cells via tumor-derived and lipid raft-associated sEVs, thereby establishing an ADO-driven immunosuppressive PMN. Targeting sEV-associated CD73 may represent a promising strategy to intercept stress-induced metastatic progression. These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for targeting CD73+ sEVs in combination with immune checkpoint blockade.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Post-COVID-19 interstitial lung abnormalities (PC-ILA) have emerged as an important component of post-COVID pulmonary sequelae in older adults, though their associated factors remain poorly defined. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 349 older adults hospitalized with COVID-19 between December 2022 and June 2024 were followed after discharge, and 265 were included in the final analysis. Patients were categorized into a PC-ILA group (n = 96) and a comparison group (n = 169). Laboratory data and Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (CGA) results obtained at admission were collected. The cohort was first divided into training and validation datasets, and candidate predictors were identified exclusively within the training dataset using baseline comparisons and LASSO regression. Three machine learning models (logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost) were established and visualized using nomogram or SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis, with performance evaluated via assessment metrics, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis with Area Under the Curve (AUC) calculation, calibration curve plotting, and clinical decision curve analysis. RESULTS: In the final analytic cohort, 96 of 265 patients (36.2%) met the study definition of PC-ILA. Eight candidate predictors were identified through differential analysis and LASSO regression, including C-reactive protein (CRP), Interleukin-6 (IL-6), IL-1β, Tumor Necrosis Factor-α (TNF-α), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), the Mini Nutritional Assessment Scale-Short Form (MNA-SF) score, the Activities of Daily Living (ADL) score and the Fried Frailty Scale score. The logistic regression model showed the most favorable overall predictive performance in the validation dataset, with the highest AUC (0.747, 95% confidence interval: 0.639-0.856) and a relatively favorable balance across accuracy, sensitivity, and F1 score. LDH, frailty, and inflammatory markers were identified as important predictors of PC-ILA. CONCLUSION: We developed an exploratory prediction framework integrating laboratory and CGA results to assess PC-ILA risk in older COVID-19 patients. The models may support early risk stratification and individualized follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) comprises genetically close nontuberculous mycobacteria responsible for human and animal infections worldwide. Increasing availability of whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data offers new opportunities for genomic surveillance and lineage tracking of these pathogens. However, the taxonomy of the MAC remains unstable, with inconsistent species and subspecies boundaries that hinder reproducible genome-based identification complicating diagnostics and antimicrobial management. Furthermore, a major barrier to the clinical and epidemiological integration of WGS is the current lack of standardized, accessible identification tools capable of translating complex genomic similarity into harmonized taxonomic assignments. METHODS: We performed a comprehensive in silico analysis of 2,737 MAC genomes using pairwise average nucleotide identity (ANI). Species and subspecies boundaries were statistically modeled at 95% and 98% ANI thresholds. A consensus genome-based framework combining FastANI and dRep clustering was developed. Machine learning classifiers based on k-mer frequency profiles were trained to reproduce genomic delineations. RESULTS: Fifteen species-level clusters were identified, with 99.9% concordance to GTDB-Tk reference classifications. Within M. avium, subsp. avium, subsp. hominissuis, and subsp. silvaticum formed a single genomic continuum, while the IS900-positive M. avium subsp. avium lineage paratuberculosis remained distinct but did not reach subspecies level divergence. Within M. intracellulare, subsp. chimaera showed deep internal structure, supporting recognition of M. intracellulare subsp. yongonense, whereas genomes assigned to M. paraintracellulare clustered within M. intracellulare subsp. intracellulare. Several nominal species (M. bouchedurhonense, M. timonense) lacked genomic coherence. The MAC displayed an open pangenome (191,904 gene clusters; 0.8% universal core). Machine learning classifiers trained on k-mer frequency profiles accurately reproduced whole-genome delineations, achieving near-perfect performances (Cohen's kappa = 0.994). CONCLUSIONS: We provide a standardized, genome-based framework for classification of the MAC and implement it in MAC-Explorer (https://mycobacteriaexplorer.fr), an open-access web tool for automated MAC identification. By integrating k-mer-based classification and insertion sequence screening, MAC-Explorer delivers reproducible and harmonized species- and lineage-level assignments, providing a robust foundation for genome-based identification and lineage tracking of MAC isolates.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To identify latent profiles based on motivation, opportunity, ability and self-reported activity behaviour in adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and examine overall participation levels, domain configurations and associations with nursing indicators. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional secondary analysis included 402 adults with a clinical diagnosis of COPD from four hospitals in Wuhan, China; spirometry results were not available for diagnostic confirmation. Latent profile analysis was conducted on sample-standardised means of four domains from a 32-item scale, with model fit, classification quality, and sensitivity to starting values and covariance specifications assessed. Six nursing risk scores were drawn from the electronic health record (EHR): the first standardised nursing risk assessment of the index admission for participants recruited during hospitalisation; the most recent traceable hospitalisation record before enrolment for outpatients. Covariate-adjusted models with HC3-robust standard errors were fitted to each score. RESULTS: The retained EVI four-profile solution comprised relatively lower ability (n=55), relatively lower opportunity with preserved ability (n=101), intermediate overall level with relatively lower motivation (n=195), and higher overall level with relatively lower behaviour (n=51). Classes 1 and 2 had similar overall levels but contrasting relative ability and opportunity. Recovery from the unweighted four-domain mean and the 32-item total score was incomplete (adjusted Rand index [ARI] 0.529 and 0.610); repeated estimation under the EVI specification closely reproduced the original assignments (ARI 0.993). Alternative covariance specifications yielded different partitions. The recorded tube-dislodgement risk score was higher in Class 1 than Class 3 (standardised contrast 0.64, 95% CI 0.35-0.93); other EHR associations were mostly null or inconsistent. Non-nested profile-versus-total-score comparisons showed no clear advantage, while separate nested analyses yielded small exploratory in-sample gains for some scores. CONCLUSION: Under the specified EVI model, the four profiles described differences in participation level and domain configuration. Their clinical utility requires prospective evaluation with objectively measured activity and appropriately timed clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary infections remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. However, conventional microbiological tests (CMTs) frequently fail to identify the causative pathogens, owing to their limited sensitivity, prolonged turnaround times, and inherent inability to detect fastidious or emerging organisms. In this context, targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) has emerged as a promising molecular approach, enabling rapid, sensitive, and comprehensive detection of respiratory pathogens directly from clinical specimens. OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the clinical application of tNGS in the etiological diagnosis of pulmonary infections. This study aimed to systematically characterize the pathogen spectrum, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) gene distribution, and infection-related immune cytokine dynamics in these patients. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients with pulmonary infections who underwent bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) testing using tNGS between August 2023 and July 2024. We performed a clinical evaluation of tNGS findings and compared its diagnostic performance with that of CMTs for pathogen identification. RESULTS: The analysis of tNGS results from 733 clinical specimens revealed a pathogen detection positivity rate of 95.63%, with 113 distinct potential pathogens identified among 701 tNGS-positive cases. Bacterial pathogens showed the highest detection rate (70.90%), and bacterial-viral coinfection emerged as the predominant mixed infection pattern (37.84%). Clinical evaluation demonstrated high concordance (91.58%) between tNGS results and initial diagnoses. Notably, tNGS facilitated the identification of mixed infections in 55 patients, leading to subsequent adjustments to antimicrobial therapy. A significant disparity was observed in the overall pathogen detection rates between tNGS and CMTs (95.63% vs. 47.07%, p < 0.001), with tNGS exhibiting superior sensitivity for the identification of bacterial, fungal, viral, and atypical pathogens. Among the 340 specimens that showed concordant positivity in tNGS and CMT results, 268 cases (78.82%) showed complete or partial diagnostic agreement. Additionally, tNGS detected antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in 198 samples, with the 23 S ribosomal RNA A2063G mutation being the most prevalent. Analysis of antimicrobial resistance revealed a strong genotype-phenotype correlation, with complete concordance observed in 69.9% of cases. Among 197 tNGS-positive cases with elevated cytokines, the infection types were characterized by a predominance of mixed over single infections. IL-6 was the most commonly elevated cytokine, and 31.98% of samples exhibited synchronous multi-cytokine elevation. CONCLUSION: tNGS demonstrated superior diagnostic performance over CMTs for the etiological diagnosis of pulmonary infections, enabling high-resolution detection of pathogens, mixed infections, and clinically relevant antimicrobial resistance genes, thereby contributing to more precise antimicrobial therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has emerged as an important biomarker for evaluating the prognosis of several respiratory diseases. However, there is currently limited research on the correlation between RAR and mortality in patients with bronchial asthma. METHODS: This study employed a multicentre cohort design: (1) The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) cohort: comprising 5,365 adult asthma patients, the study analysed the independent association between RAR and mortality using methods such as the Cox proportional hazards model and restricted cubic splines (RCS); (2) The MIMIC-IV cohort: comprising 1,474 ICU patients with asthma, this cohort assessed the independent predictive value of RAR for 30-day all-cause mortality, evaluated its incremental value, and utilised a group-based trajectory model (GBTM) to identify the longitudinal trajectory of RAR over time and its association with prognosis; (3) eICU-CRD cohort: comprising 859 ICU patients with asthma, to validate the consistency of the aforementioned associations in a multicentre setting; (4) NWICU cohort: comprising 177 ICU patients with asthma, to assess robustness across databases and time periods specific to the database. RESULTS: In NHANES, each one‑unit increase in RAR was associated with a 71% higher risk of all‑cause mortality (HR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.46-2.00). RCS showed a non‑linear positive association (inflection point: 3.13); Q4 vs. Q1 conferred a 125% higher risk (HR = 2.25). In MIMIC‑IV, RAR independently predicted 30‑day mortality (HR = 1.23); adding RAR to SAPS II improved AUC from 0.787 to 0.810 (ΔAUC = 0.023, P < 0.001). Trajectory analysis identified three patterns; patients with persistently high RAR had a 2.25‑fold higher death risk (HR = 2.25). Each unit increase in RAR was associated with a 21% higher mortality risk (HR = 1.21, 95% CI: 1.14-1.29, P < 0.001) in eICU‑CRD and a 42% higher mortality risk (HR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.11-1.81, P = 0.005) in NWICU. CONCLUSIONS: RAR is non-linearly positively associated with mortality in patients with bronchial asthma and has both static and dynamic prognostic value; however, this requires further validation through prospective studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Nuclear protein in testis (NUT) carcinoma is a rare, highly aggressive cancer driven by NUTM1 rearrangements and typically arises in the midline structures. Prognosis is poor, and emerging evidence suggests primary tumor sites influence outcomes. This study compares overall and cancer-specific survival among adults with NUT carcinoma in the nasal cavity/paranasal sinuses (NUT NCS) with lung/bronchus (NUT LB). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the SEER database with histologically confirmed NUT carcinoma. Patients were categorized by primary site (NCS vs. LB). Covariates included age, sex, and stage at diagnosis. Survival outcomes were analyzed by using Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression. RESULTS: Of 127 patients, 77 had LB and 50 had NCS primaries. LB tumors were more common in younger patients (55.8% aged 19-49 vs. 38.0%; p = 0.009). NCS tumors more frequently presented with T4 disease (76% vs. 53.3%; p = 0.030), whereas LB tumors more frequently exhibited N1-N3 nodal disease (71.5% vs. 30%; p < 0.001) and distant metastasis (53.3% vs. 16%; p < 0.001). Unadjusted survival did not differ by site. In multivariable analysis, LB showed a higher overall mortality (HR 1.84, 95% CI 1.07-3.16) and cancer-specific mortality (HR 2.10, 95% CI 1.14-3.89). CONCLUSIONS: Pulmonary NUT carcinoma showed more disseminated disease and worse adjusted survival than NCS. Primary site appears prognostically relevant, although findings are limited by registry constraints and treatment confounding.

papers.abstract_en: Lipid peroxidation and pyroptotic activation both contribute to airway epithelial injury, but their temporal relationship and reciprocal effects remain incompletely defined. This study examined the contribution of the cystine/glutamate antiporter xCT to these responses in cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-exposed bronchial epithelial cells. BEAS-2B cells were exposed to CSE (0%-10%) for 0-48 h, with selected observations repeated in 16HBE cells. Redox status, membrane injury, pyroptosis-associated proteins and intracellular and extracellular glutathione were measured. Pharmacological interventions were combined with xCT, GSDMD, NLRP3 and CASP1 silencing. Independent siRNAs validated the xCT and GSDMD responses. xCT turnover was examined by cycloheximide chase and ubiquitin immunoblotting. xCT protein decreased by 24.7% and C11-BODIPY oxidation increased 1.60-fold at 6 h (both p < 0.001); measured pyroptotic proteins first increased significantly at 12 h. An independent SLC7A11 siRNA reproduced the increases in GSDMD-N, cleaved caspase-1, MDA and LDH release. NLRP3 or CASP1 silencing reduced GSDMD-N, interleukin-1β and LDH. GSDMD inhibition decreased extracellular GSH and preserved intracellular redox status without restoring xCT. Mean xCT half-life decreased from 10.54 h in controls to 4.12 h under CSE and increased to 8.07 h with MG132. Nigericin attenuated ferrostatin-1- and disulfiram-associated protection. xCT turnover is associated with an early lipid-peroxidation response followed by NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD-associated injury. Independent genetic interventions support contributions of xCT and GSDMD to reciprocal redox-inflammatory responses, including GSDMD-associated glutathione release.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Although systemic exposure to anti-tuberculosis agents is critical for therapeutic efficacy, substantial inter-individual variability of drug exposure persists despite standardized dosing. Emerging studies suggest that the gut microbiota may influence drug metabolism and host pharmacokinetics, yet the role of the gut microbiota in driving pharmacokinetic variability in the context of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) remains unclear. In this prospective cohort study, we aimed to examine whether pre-treatment gut microbial composition and functional capacity shape drug exposure in patients with MDR-TB. METHODS: We enrolled patients with MDR-TB at designated TB medical institutions in Suzhou, Jiangsu Province. Fecal samples were collected prior to anti-tuberculosis treatment for metagenomic sequencing, and blood samples were obtained after two weeks of treatment to estimate the drug exposure levels of levofloxacin, linezolid, bedaquiline, clofazimine, and cycloserine. The relationship between gut microbiota features and drug exposure was assessed using MaAsLin2 to identify microbial species, metabolic pathways, and enzymes associated with drug metabolism. RESULTS: Pronounced dysbiosis, characterized by reduced alpha diversity and a decrease in anaerobic bacteria abundance accompanied by an increase in facultative anaerobes, was associated with lower plasma exposure to levofloxacin, linezolid, bedaquiline, clofazimine, and cycloserine. Metagenomic functional profiling indicated that biosynthesis pathways for amino acid and peptidoglycan were enriched in individuals with higher drug exposure, while degradation pathways for these compounds were more prevalent in those with lower exposure. Specific species positively associated with drug exposure encoded genes for the enzymes involved in the biosynthesis pathways for amino acid and peptidoglycan. CONCLUSIONS: Analyses demonstrate that pre-treatment dysbiosis is associated with lower systemic exposure to anti-TB drugs. These findings suggest a potential link between gut microbiota composition and drug exposure variability, though causality remains to be established. Further research is needed to determine whether microbiota-targeted strategies could influence pharmacokinetics and improve MDR-TB treatment outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility and interobserver reproducibility of a noncontrast multiparametric chest magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) protocol in patients with connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD), and to assess its association with computed tomography (CT)-based quantitative fibrosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 28 patients with CTD-ILD underwent noncontrast chest MRI including ultrashort echo-time (UTE) lung imaging, pulmonary trunk flow, cine ventricular function, and lung T2 mapping. Three blinded thoracic radiologists independently assessed MR-visible pulmonary fibrosis. Interobserver agreement for MR-visible fibrosis was evaluated. Exploratory analyses assessed the agreement between MR-visible fibrosis, CT-based quantitative fibrosis (QILD), and pulmonary function tests. RESULTS: All 28 patients completed the planned MRI protocol (100%). Interpretable images were obtained in all patients for pulmonary trunk flow and cine ventricular imaging, and in 27 of 28 patients (96.4%) for UTE lung imaging and lung T2 mapping. The mean total scan time was 56.9 ±13.2 minutes. The proportion of patients with MR-visible fibrosis ranged from 81.5% to 96.3% across readers, notably higher than the CT-quantified disease burden in this cohort (median QILD, 1.2%). Interobserver agreement was fair to moderate across features (Fleiss' κ = 0.357-0.488). The extent of MR-visible fibrosis demonstrated a significant positive correlation with QILD (Spearman ρ = 0.568, P = 0.002). Lung T2 mapping values also correlated positively with QILD (ρ = 0.591, P = 0.001). CONCLUSION: Noncontrast multiparametric chest MRI is feasible in patients with CTD-ILD, providing interpretable lung and cardiopulmonary imaging within a single examination. Interobserver agreement for MR-visible fibrosis was fair to moderate, and fibrosis extent and T2 mapping values correlated with CT-based quantitative fibrosis, supporting further investigation of MRI as a radiation-sparing imaging option, pending longitudinal validation, in CTD-ILD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Abnormal lipid metabolism is widely recognized as a hallmark of cancer cells. In particular, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells exhibit heightened lipid metabolic processes to meet their biosynthetic and energetic demands, while concurrently reprogramming lipid metabolism to remodel the tumour microenvironment (TME). MAIN BODY: This review details the pivotal roles of lipid metabolic reprogramming in NSCLC. First, we delineate the distinct lipid metabolic characteristics of NSCLC, exploring their regulatory mechanisms and contributions to tumour progression. Given the significant impact of lipids on the TME, we subsequently describe the intricate crosstalk between NSCLC cells and other cellular components within the TME. Furthermore, we investigate the relationship between lipid metabolism and NSCLC treatment, encompassing its role in therapeutic resistance and the potential of targeting lipid metabolism as a therapeutic strategy. Finally, we discuss the prospects and current limitations of targeting lipid metabolism in the clinical management of NSCLC. CONCLUSIONS: A substantial body of evidence suggests that lipid metabolic reprogramming plays a critical role in NSCLC. Median time to progression data from a phase I clinical study demonstrated that monotherapy with the FASN inhibitor showed a preliminary signal of clinical activity in KRAS-mutant NSCLC (64% remained progression-free for > 12 weeks, n = 11) compared with KRAS-wildtype NSCLC (0% >12 weeks, n = 6; p < 0.02). However, to date, no lipid-targeted therapy has demonstrated clinically meaningful efficacy in unselected NSCLC patients. Targeting dysregulated lipid metabolism in NSCLC is supported by extensive preclinical rationale, but clinical validation remains limited to specific molecular subtypes. Realising the therapeutic potential of this strategy will require addressing fundamental gaps in target selectivity, tumour-type specificity, and clinical validation. Further studies should focus on elucidating the lipid metabolic networks in NSCLC to enhance treatment outcomes for affected patients.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Dysregulation of the fibrinolytic system is increasingly recognized as a key driver of pulmonary fibrosis pathogenesis and progression. Here, we systematically evaluated systemic and local fibrinolytic status across distinct interstitial lung disease (ILD) phenotypes. METHODS: We conducted a single-center observational study and measured plasma and induced sputum levels of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA), and urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA) via ELISA in 141 ILD patients and 39 healthy controls. Patients were stratified into fibrotic and non-fibrotic subtypes; systemic and local fibrinolytic profiles were compared, with subgroup, inter-marker correlation, and survival analyses. RESULTS: PAI-1 was significantly elevated in both plasma and sputum of the fibrotic ILD group (P < 0.05). Plasma tPA was elevated across all ILD patients. By contrast, sputum tPA was elevated only in the fibrotic ILD group, where levels were significantly higher than those in both the non-fibrotic ILD group and healthy controls. Sputum uPA was upregulated in all ILD patients (P < 0.0001 and P < 0.0001). Correlation analysis revealed a significant association between PAI-1 and tPA in plasma, and between PAI-1 and uPA in sputum. In an exploratory survival analysis of 112 patients with ILD and available sputum samples (11 deaths over up to 700 days of follow-up), elevated sputum PAI-1 was associated with increased mortality risk (HR = 4.513; 95% CI: 1.38-14.72; P = 0.0344). CONCLUSIONS: Plasma and induced sputum concentrations of fibrinolytic markers showed distinct patterns across groups in fibrotic ILD, suggesting biomarker associations. In exploratory analysis, elevated sputum PAI-1 was associated with increased mortality, a finding that warrants confirmation in larger studies.
