papers.abstract_en: Anti-tuberculosis (TB) drugs must reach the disease site to be effective, but complex TB pathology limits drug distribution and efficacy, as bacteria in the necrotic center of lung cavities are difficult to access and kill. Our study generates the most comprehensive database of site-of-disease distribution for 24 drugs and drug candidates in a rabbit model of cavitary TB. We validate a lung lesion penetration model with clinical data and develop an integrated approach that combines microenvironment-specific pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Next, we simulate site-of-disease coverage of shortened regimens tested in major Phase 3 trials over the past decade, allowing direct comparisons with trial outcomes. We propose that regimens including at least two drugs achieving bactericidal concentrations in pulmonary cavities are more likely to meet primary clinical endpoints in patients with cavitary disease. Our translational platform constitutes a validated tool to support drug evaluation, smart regimen design, and de-risking of late-stage trials.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Clinical Immune Phenotyping and Explainable Risk Modeling for Lung Cancer (CIPHER-Lung) is a rule-based peripheral blood immune score that organizes measured biomarkers into clinically readable concepts. We assessed whether these concepts outperform constituent markers, remain stable under assay-like computational perturbations, and identify discordance with standard disease burden. METHODS: This retrospective exploratory internal evaluation used 260 sample records from de-identified participants in an existing institutional cohort. Overall-survival analyses included 162 patients with lung cancer and 73 deaths, and only 31 had all six markers. The primary available-concept score combined the measured subset of a six-marker panel into four phenotypic proxies: loss of T-cell surveillance, checkpoint activation/terminal differentiation, cytokine inflammation, and hematology/myeloid inflammation. The fixed formula was applied without outcome-based coefficient refitting. Analyses included matched marker comparisons, clinical benchmarking, inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted (IPCW) evaluation, concept ablation, limited adaptation, computational jitter dropout, and 24-month discordance phenotyping. RESULTS: The available-concept score had a Harrell C-index of 0.697 and IPCW cumulative/dynamic AUROCs of 0.765 and 0.764 at 12 and 24 months. On matched participants, the composite exceeded CD3, CD8+PD-1+, CD8+CD57+, and the cytokine concept, whereas the NLR/hematology concept performed similarly in its smaller subset. The supplied fixed weighting did not outperform unweighted aggregation. Training-fold calibration and a four-concept linear probe produced only modest gains over the fixed score. Under five-point concept jitter plus 10% dropout, the median C-index was 0.691, rank correlation was 0.939, and high-risk agreement was 0.912. Descriptive point estimates were higher for clinical models. The combined model showed no material point-estimate gain over the clinical model. Paired intervals for clinical-model comparisons were unavailable. CONCLUSIONS: CIPHER-Lung provides an interpretable immune-state representation supported by this retrospective exploratory internal evaluation. The score is not supported for stand-alone diagnosis, treatment selection, or replacement of stage and performance status. Candidate uses in longitudinal phenotyping, enrichment, or point-of-care reporting require complete-marker multicenter validation, documented reference standards, analytical qualification, external calibration, and prospective impact studies.

papers.title_en: A real-world study based on targeted next-generation sequencing: association of cytomegalovirus detection with co-detection of Pneumocystis jirovecii and Aspergillus fumigatus in respiratory patients.
papers.authors: Lin Y, Wu X, Zhang W, Zhang L, Wu Z
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, Zhangzhou Municipal Hospital of Fujian Province and Zhangzhou Affi…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) are among the most common and lethal infectious diseases globally, with approximately 50% lacking a definitive etiological diagnosis. Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) shows promise in pulmonary infection diagnosis. Human herpesviruses, including Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV), can reactivate in immunocompromised individuals and are closely linked to the co-detection of opportunistic pathogens. OBJECTIVE: Based on 1156 samples, we evaluated the detection rates of EBV and CMV, explored the co-detection associations between CMV positivity and Pneumocystis jirovecii and Aspergillus fumigatus, and examined the modifying effect of age. METHODS: A total of 1156 patients who underwent tNGS at the Respiratory Department of Zhangzhou Hospital (December 2024-April 2026) were enrolled (38 duplicate samples were excluded). Standard Pearson's chi-square tests (without continuity correction; Fisher's exact test when expected frequency < 5) were used. Odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated, and the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied. Multivariable logistic regression (adjusted for age and sex) and interaction analyses were conducted to evaluate independent associations and age-modifying effects. RESULTS: EBV (42.1% vs. 33.2%, P = 0.0016) and CMV (29.3% vs. 16.3%, P < 0.0001) detection rates were significantly higher in the elderly group. In the overall population, P. jirovecii detection was significantly increased in CMV-positive patients (OR = 1.72, 95% CI 1.12-2.59, P = 0.011). The strongest CMV-A. fumigatus association was observed in the non-elderly group (OR = 2.46, 95% CI 1.32-4.42, P = 0.003). Interaction analysis showed that age significantly modified the CMV-A. fumigatus association (interaction P = 0.027), whereas the CMV-P. jirovecii association remained robust across age groups (interaction P = 0.194). CMV/EBV showed no significant association with non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) (all adjusted P > 0.05). CONCLUSION: CMV positivity was significantly associated with the co-detection of P. jirovecii in the overall population and A. fumigatus in non-elderly patients, suggesting that CMV detection may serve as a warning signal prompting opportunistic pathogen screening. Age is a significant effect modifier of the CMV-A. fumigatus association. Of note, the present findings reflect microbiological co-detection rather than clinical co-infection.

papers.title_en: Effectiveness of Aerobic Exercise on Functional Capacity, Quality of Life and Pulmonary Function in COPD Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Trial Sequential Analysis.

papers.affiliation_highlight: College of Rehabilitation Medicine, Fujian University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Fuzhou, Fujian, People's Republic…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Aerobic exercise is a central component of Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR), but the aerobic exercise remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of aerobic exercise on functional capacity, quality of life, and pulmonary function in COPD patients. METHODS: We systematically searched eight electronic databases from inception to January 2026 for English and Chinese RCTs. Inclusion and exclusion criteria included COPD patients, pure aerobic exercise, RCTs and outcome measures. Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool 2 (RoB2) assessed risk of bias. Meta-analysis was conducted using RevMan 5.3 and Stata 17.0. GRADE evaluated certainty of evidence. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) assessed evidence robustness. This study has been registered with PROSPERO under ID CRD42022377652. RESULTS: 2043 participants were included in 26 RCTs. Aerobic exercises had significant improvements on 6MWT (MD 38.78, 95% CI 28.87-48.68, 95%PI -1.96 to 79.52), CAT (MD -4.26, 95% CI -5.80 to -2.71, 95%PI -10.03 to 1.52), SGRQ (MD -8.96, 95% CI -12.26 to -5.65, 95%PI-21.66 to 3.75), FEV1%pred (MD 5.98, 95% CI 3.61-8.35, 95%PI -1.60 to 13.56), and FEV1/FVC% (MD 3.76, 95% CI 2.47-5.06, 95%PI 0.08 to 7.45). GRADE rated evidence as moderate for 6MWT, CAT, SGRQ, and FEV1/FVC%, but low for FEV1%pred. TSA confirmed robust and conclusive evidence for CAT, SGRQ, FEV1%pred and FEV1/FVC%, while the evidence for 6MWT was supportive but not conclusive. CONCLUSION: Aerobic exercise improves functional capacity (6MWT), health-related quality of life (CAT, SGRQ) and pulmonary function (FEV1/FVC%, FEV1%pred) in patients with COPD, with primary outcomes exceeding the MCID and supported by moderate-certainty evidence (low for FEV1%pred); however, 95% prediction intervals cross the null for all outcomes except FEV1/FVC%, indicating variable effects across clinical settings. Given residual heterogeneity and short-term follow-up, long-term well-designed RCTs are needed to confirm the sustainability of these benefits.

papers.title_en: Effects of cryo-parameters and retrieval methods on specimen acquisition and quality for ultrathin cryoprobe transbronchial cryobiopsy in porcine models.
papers.authors: Ye L, Hong S, Huang Z, Chen J, Xie F, Zhu L, Liu S, Xi H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory Endoscopy, Shanghai Chest Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ultrathin cryoprobes enable direct retraction through the working channel during transbronchial cryobiopsy. However, key factors of biopsy performance remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluates cryo-parameters and retrieval methods across different working channels in a porcine model to define parameter strategies that balance specimen acquisition, quality and complication risk. METHODS: Transbronchial cryobiopsy using an ultrathin cryoprobe under different cryo-parameters was compared with standard forceps biopsy (sFB) in ex vivo and in vivo models. Biopsy approaches were classified into five groups: P290 (BF-P290, cryoprobe retracted through 2.0 mm diameter working channel), EWC (BF-1TQ290 combined with a 2.0 mm diameter extending working channel (EWC), cryoprobe retracted through the EWC), 1TQ290-IN (BF-1TQ290, cryoprobe retracted through 3.0 mm diameter working channel), 1TQ290-OUT (BF-1TQ290, cryoprobe retracted en bloc with the bronchoscope), and sFB (standard forceps biopsy with BF-1TQ290). Acquisition rates, specimen quality and complications were assessed. RESULTS: In ex vivo experiments at 55 and 60 bar, a 3 s cryo-activation time was sufficient to produce specimens of greater size than those obtained with sFB. In vivo, cryo-activation times of 3-7 s achieved acquisition rates > 60% across all groups. At 9 s, acquisition rates declined to < 60% for EWC and P290, whereas the 1TQ290-IN and 1TQ290-OUT groups maintained rates > 60%. Except for the EWC group at 3 s, all groups had greater specimen weight, macroscopic cross-sectional areas, and microscopic section areas than sFB (P < 0.05). No severe complications (grade ≥ 3 bleeding) occurred; grade 2 bleeding and pneumothorax were predominantly observed in the 1TQ290-IN and 1TQ290-OUT groups at cryo-activation times 7 and 9 s. CONCLUSIONS: For ultrathin cryoprobe transbronchial cryobiopsy with retraction through the EWC, a cryo-activation time of 5-7 s appears to yield increased specimen size compared with sFB, while maintaining a high specimen acquisition rate (> 60%) and procedural safety. For withdrawal via P290 and 1TQ290 bronchoscope's working channels, a 3-7 s appears to provide a favorable balance between specimen acquisition rate, quality and procedural safety.

papers.title_en: Serum CEA, CA 19 - 9, and FDG PET/CT SUVmax in relation to histological subtype and overall survival in stage IV lung cancer.
papers.authors: Aydin S, Gencer G, Balci A, Kekilli E, Sen S
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Faculty of Medicine, Afyonkarahisar Health Sciences University, Afyonkarahisar, Türkiye.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This retrospective study investigated the association of serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and carbohydrate antigen 19 - 9 (CA 19 - 9) levels with 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG PET/CT) findings, histological subtype, and overall survival in patients with stage IV lung cancer. This is an observational, hypothesis-generating analysis; no diagnostic accuracy metrics (sensitivity, specificity, or ROC/AUC) were computed. METHODS: A total of 217 patients with stage IV lung cancer were included in the analysis. Clinical data collected comprised tumor size, histopathological subtype, maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) obtained from FDG PET/CT, and serum CEA and CA 19 - 9 levels. Correlations among these variables and their relationships with survival outcomes were analyzed using IBM SPSS, and graphical visualizations were generated using Python. Statistical significance was established at P < 0.05. RESULTS: The cohort comprised 217 patients (196 males and 21 females; median age, 64 years [IQR, 56-72]), including 79 (36.4%) with adenocarcinoma, 94 (43.3%) with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), and 44 (20.3%) with small cell lung cancer (SCLC). Median CEA was 3.78 ng/mL (IQR, 2.25-7.25), median CA 19 - 9 was 13.95 U/mL (IQR, 7.09-21.50), and median SUVmax was 14.40 (IQR, 9.30-18.80). Median serum 19 - 9, CEA/CA 19 - 9 ratio, and SUVmax did not differ significantly across histological subtypes (Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.942, 0.983, 0.838, and 0.326, respectively). Tumor size differed significantly across subtypes (Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.024), with the highest median value observed in the SCLC group. Median overall survival did not differ significantly across histological subtypes (Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.341; log-rank P = 0.312) or between sexes (Mann-Whitney U P = 0.942; log-rank P = 0.544). Apart from the mathematically expected correlations between the CEA/CA 19 - 9 ratio and its component biomarkers, Spearman correlation analysis identified only weak unadjusted associations, none of which remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. To avoid multicollinearity arising from the simultaneous inclusion of 19 - 9, and their arithmetically derived ratio, two separate multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were constructed. Older age was the only independent adverse prognostic factor in both models (aHR ≈ 1.03 per year, P = 0.001); serum biomarkers, SUVmax, tumor size, sex, and histological subtype were not independently associated with overall survival. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective stage IV lung cancer cohort, serum CEA, CA 19 - 9, and PET/CT SUVmax did not differ significantly across histological subtypes and were not independently associated with overall survival after adjustment for the covariates available in the multivariable Cox models. Older age was the only independent adverse prognostic factor identified in both models. These findings should not be interpreted as demonstrating an absence of prognostic value of these parameters in stage IV lung cancer in general, because several established clinical and molecular prognostic factors were unavailable for adjustment. The results are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and require validation in prospectively characterized cohorts.

papers.title_zh: The effects of dexamethasone on the behavior and neurotransmitters of asthmatic model mice.
papers.title_en: The effects of dexamethasone on the behavior and neurotransmitters of asthmatic model mice.
papers.authors: Wu MY, Zhu HF, Ma SL, Zhang L, Ding XY
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pediatrics, Pudong New Area People's Hospital, Shanghai, 201299, China.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with acute asthma frequently present with both neurological and psychological manifestations. Changes in neurotransmitter levels may provide objective indicators for assessing behavioral status. This study was conducted to investigate the effects of dexamethasone on motor behavior, neurotransmitter levels, and inflammatory mediators in a murine asthma model. Dopamine (DA), acetylcholine (ACh), γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and interleukin-4 (IL-4) were measured to assess neuroimmune interactions. METHODS: Twenty-four C57 mice were randomly assigned to control, asthma, and treatment groups. Mice were initially sensitized with Der p1 and subsequently challenged with house dust mite (HDM) extract. Mice in the treatment group received dexamethasone (1 mg/kg) before challenge, after which motor behavior was evaluated using the open field test. ELISA was used to measure IL-4, TNF-α, GABA, and DA in plasma; IL-4 and TNF-α in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF); and TNF-α, GABA, DA, and ACh in brain tissue. RESULTS: Compared with the asthma group, the treatment group showed significantly reduced IL-4 and TNF-α levels in BALF (all P < 0.05). Plasma GABA and DA levels were increased, whereas plasma IL-4 and TNF-α levels were decreased (all P < 0.05). In brain tissue, ACh and TNF-α levels were decreased, whereas GABA and DA levels were increased (all P < 0.05). In the open field test, the total distance traveled, the proportion of time spent in the central area and speed in the peripheral area of the asthma group were all lower than those of the treatment group, while time spent in the peripheral area was higher than that of the treatment group (all P < 0.05). Correlation analysis showed that IL-4, TNF-α, and brain ACh levels were negatively correlated with total movement distance, time spent in the central area, mean speed in the central area, and mean speed in the peripheral area (all P < 0.05). Plasma DA levels were positively correlated with these behavioral indicators (all P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: Locomotor and exploratory behavior in asthmatic mice was improved by dexamethasone. The therapeutic effect of dexamethasone on asthma-associated behavioral changes may be associated with concurrent modulation of neurotransmitter levels and suppression of Th cell-related inflammatory mediators.

papers.abstract_en: Referral of people with chronic respiratory disease to pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) remains low despite program benefits. We aimed to explore patient and health professional (HP) experiences of the PR referral process, to identify and co-design strategies to support referral. Focus groups and qualitative interviews were conducted in Phase 1, and a co-design workshop in Phase 2. Phase 1 included 14 people with lived experience and 10 HPs. Participants reported different experiences of the referral process highlighting patient expectation of only brief information about PR at the time of referral. Resources to promote PR awareness and knowledge, referral feedback, and HP education were developed in Phase 2 with inputs from two people with lived experience, three HPs and PR clinicians. In this study, participants identified new strategies to support referral to PR including the use of referral acknowledgement and focussed end rehabilitation feedback, and novel suggestions for HP education.

papers.abstract_en: Pseudomonas aeruginosa: is one of the predominant pathogens associated with cystic fibrosis (CF) airway infections. Treatment is often challenging due to its intrinsic multidrug resistance, particularly because of the activity of tripartite resistance-nodulation-division (RND) drug efflux pumps such as the MexAB-OprM system. We have previously shown that ivacaftor, a cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) potentiator used in CF therapy, could enhance antibiotic activity against Escherichia coli through inhibition of the AcrB drug efflux protein. Given the high level of homology between the resistance-nodulation-division (RND) transporters from the drug efflux complexes, AcrB and MexB, the aim of this study was to investigate if ivacaftor could also synergise with antibiotics used to treat Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections in people with cystic fibrosis. Molecular dynamics simulation interrogated the interaction between ivacaftor and MexB. Thermal shift analysis and surface plasmon resonance were employed to determine the affinity of ivacaftor binding to MexB. The effects of ivacaftor on antibiotic susceptibility, efflux activity, and membrane integrity were investigated for reference strains and clinical P. aeruginosa strains isolated from people with CF. Our results predicted binding of ivacaftor to the distal binding site of MexB. Ivacaftor interacted with the RND transporters AcrB and MexB with a similar affinity as the efflux pump inhibitor (EPI) phenylalanine-arginine beta-naphthylamide (PAβN). Checkerboard assays demonstrated that ivacaftor restored susceptibility to several antibiotics currently used in anti-pseudomonal CF therapy, particularly aztreonam, ceftazidime, ciprofloxacin, and meropenem, while enhancing the antibiotic activity of azithromycin, erythromycin and minocycline. Nile Red efflux and Hoechst 33342 accumulation assays further supported inhibition of efflux activity by ivacaftor. Ivacaftor did not produce any off-target effects on the bacterial inner- or outer membrane. Overall, the results suggest that ivacaftor can function as an EPI in P. aeruginosa, thereby enhancing antibiotic activity. These findings support further investigation of CFTR modulators as adjunctive therapies against chronic infections caused by multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer still remains the world's top cause of cancer-related deaths, and the need for safe, multi-targeted preventative and complementary methods is highlighted by the limitation of current treatments, including toxicity, resistance, and late detection. Citrus plant-derived phytochemicals have gained attention because of their exceptional safety profiles, biological activity, and chemical diversity. The beneficial effects of citrus phytochemicals in the prevention and treatment of lung cancer are supported by molecular, preclinical, and translational data rigorously evaluated in this review. In non-small cell lung cancer models, particularly in A549 and H1299 cells, citrus flavonoids such as hesperidin, naringenin, naringin, and nobiletin exhibit dose-dependent cytotoxicity with IC50 values of around 25-50 µM. Their anticancer effects are achieved by cell-cycle arrest, activation of mitochondrial apoptosis, and suppression of EGFR, PI3K/AKT, MAPK/ERK, and JAK2/STAT3 signaling. Citrus phytochemicals affect angiogenesis, the epithelial-mesenchymal transition, cancer stemness, lipid metabolism, and epigenetic regulators such as HDACs, DNMTs, and oncogenic microRNAs in addition to rendering cytotoxicity. Their translational value is further supported by epidemiological studies that show an approximately 9% lower risk of lung cancer with a citrus-rich diet. The promise of citrus phytochemicals as integrative agents in lung cancer prevention and therapy is strengthened by developments in structure optimization and pulmonary-targeted delivery methods.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) have been proposed as mediators of the gut-lung axis in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, the human evidence is limited and heterogeneous across disease states and specimen types. We therefore synthesized the available evidence to describe reported associations between fecal or plasma SCFAs and COPD-related phenotypes and to place the proposed biological mechanisms in context. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through December 31, 2025. Five studies enrolled 333 participants, of whom 314 contributed SCFA outcome data. Quantitative pooling was not appropriate because the studies differed substantially in disease status, comparison groups, specimen types, interventions, and data formats. We therefore used descriptive statistics and qualitative trend synthesis, stratified findings by population, disease status, and specimen type, and compared interventions narratively. RESULTS: Zhu et al. reported lower levels of all measured fecal SCFAs in 24 patients with acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD) than in 18 healthy controls. Li et al. reported lower fecal acetate, isobutyrate, and isovalerate in severe stable COPD, with no significant differences in propionate or butyrate. Kirschner et al. reported lower plasma acetate in stable COPD (P = 0.001), with no significant differences in propionate or butyrate. Otake et al. found lower plasma total SCFAs and propionate in smokers than in non-smokers; acetate and butyrate did not differ significantly. Because these comparisons were not biologically or methodologically exchangeable, no cross-study effect estimate was calculated. CONCLUSION: This exploratory synthesis identified study-specific patterns of lower acetate and branched-chain SCFAs, but the patterns varied by disease state, specimen type, and comparison group. They should not be interpreted as evidence of a universal SCFA deficiency in COPD. A high-fiber diet showed beneficial effects in mouse models, whereas a three-month multi-nutrient intervention did not alter gut microbiota composition or systemic inflammation in humans. Larger prospective cohorts and adequately powered, longer-term trials are required before clinical translation can be considered.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent airflow obstruction. Cigarette smoking remains a major risk factor. In this study, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify smoking-associated genes that are associated with the pathogenesis of COPD and to computationally infer the downstream injury mechanisms through which they act. METHODS: Data on COPD and smoking were obtained from public databases. Distinct cell types in COPD were identified through single-cell analysis. Next, pivotal cell populations and candidate genes were delineated by leveraging GWAS analyses linked to single-cell phenotypic characteristics, and candidate genes were identified based on expression level analysis. The biological mechanisms underlying smoking and COPD were examined using functional enrichment and immune infiltration analyses. RESULTS: Four candidate key COPD genes were identified, including SLC34A2, SDC4, DHCR24, and MGST1, which were significantly downregulated in COPD samples. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis revealed that epithelial cells represent an important cell type in COPD, with the key genes being dynamically expressed during epithelial cell differentiation. Seven specific transcription factors were identified in epithelial cells, including RFX3, TEAD1, IRF8, SPI1, IRF8_extended, BHLHE41, and ERG. The four key genes were significantly enriched in the "Protein degradation" pathway and the KEAP1-NFE2L2 oxidative stress pathway. In addition, 23 different immune cell types were identified, and activated B cells were negatively associated with DHCR24, SDC4, and MGST1 expression. CONCLUSION: Through computational integration, we identified SLC34A2, SDC4, DHCR24, and MGST1 as candidate key genes whose expression in airway epithelial cells is associated with smoking and COPD. Computational analyses suggest that these genes are involved in mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress. These results provide a hypothesis-generating basis for future functional studies and for examining these genes as potential biomarkers, although they do not reveal therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize immune cell metabolic alterations and their regulatory mechanisms in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and to identify metabolism-related immune subtypes associated with lung dysfunction to support immunometabolic classification and targeted therapeutic strategies. METHODS: Public transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing datasets were integrated to identify key metabolic genes, classify COPD patients into molecular subtypes, and characterize immune cell metabolic profiles and regulatory networks. Untargeted serum metabolomics was performed to identify differential metabolites. A cigarette smoke-induced COPD mouse model was established, and multiple molecular and histological experiments were performed for validation. RESULTS: We identified 27 core metabolic genes and classified COPD patients into two subtypes. Subtype C1 was characterized by poorer lung function and higher infiltration of innate immune cells, with enrichment of SPP1⁺ macrophages exhibiting increased glycolytic and lipid metabolic activity. Transcription factors MITF, TCF7L2, and BHLHE41 were identified as predicted upstream regulators of the metabolic reprogramming observed in these cells, which showed increased interactions with CD8⁺ Tem and NK cells. Serum lactate and succinate levels were significantly upregulated in patients with COPD. Animal experiments further confirmed increased proportion of SPP1⁺ macrophages, elevated expression of metabolic genes, and increased levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines in COPD mice. CONCLUSION: COPD exhibits distinct immune heterogeneity characterized by altered cellular metabolism. SPP1⁺ macrophages represent a prominent myeloid subset closely associated with metabolic disorders and lung injury. These results provide a basis for immunometabolic subtyping of COPD and may inform the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In older adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), inhaler device characteristics can influence operability, adherence, and satisfaction. We evaluated short-term changes in clinical measures after switching to budesonide/glycopyrronium/formoterol (Breztri Aerosphere) in older adults with COPD. METHODS: In this single-center, open-label switch study, outpatients aged ≥65 years with COPD receiving maintenance triple therapy (inhaled corticosteroid/long-acting β2-agonist/long-acting muscarinic antagonist) were switched to budesonide/glycopyrronium/formoterol and followed for 8 weeks. COPD Assessment Test (CAT), modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale, Adherence Starts with Knowledge-20 (ASK-20), spirometry, impulse oscillometry, a study-specific questionnaire on inhaler operability and adverse symptoms, and overall satisfaction measured using a 0-100 mm visual analog scale (VAS; 0 = worst, 100 = best) were assessed. RESULTS: Twenty-five male patients were enrolled, with a median age of 81 years. Switching to budesonide/glycopyrronium/formoterol was associated with improved mMRC scores (median 1 [1-3] to 1 [1-2], p = 0.03) and decreased ASK-20 barrier counts (median 3 [1-5] to 2 [1-5], p = 0.05). CAT scores and lung function/impulse oscillometry showed no significant changes. Adverse effects were generally infrequent, and inhaler operability was rated favorably. The mean overall VAS score was 65.7 ± 16.1 mm. CONCLUSION: In this small cohort of older men with COPD, switching to budesonide/glycopyrronium/formoterol was associated with improved dyspnea and reduced adherence barriers, without frequent side effects.
